Per Owner decision #5 (binding direction, recorded in /tmp/owner_decision_T033.txt) the workflow must first route through planning (Planner -> Plan Reviewer) to merge the frozen contract with Owner decision #3 (Robinhood finality policy: use finalized tag as the formal boundary; unfinalized data is observable but must not enter the qualified dataset; finalized unavailable / fallback / abnormal / endpoint ancestry disagreement -> fail closed; confirmations=12 retained only as EXPERIMENTAL_NOT_LIVE_APPROVED fixture placeholder) and Owner decision #7 (FINALIZED_ANCESTRY_VIOLATION critical-incident definition: a previously finalized block no longer belongs to the finalized ancestry, or qualified endpoints persistently disagree on finalized block hash/ancestry; incident handling includes halt + critical-incident candidate + block new qualification/paper/live + preserve old raw partitions and all provider evidence + new fork as append-only evidence + Phase 8 operator/incident escalation + superseding canonical generation only after manual declaration + finalized raw evidence is never rewritten) into a single contract body before implementation may begin. triage_request.requested_change: Have the Planner merge Owner decisions #3 and #7 into the Outcome / Deliverables / Acceptance / Must-not / References sections of T033 and remove the dual-layer expression created by the top-of-file FROZEN_FROM_BASELINE marker. The Implementation status line must clearly state T033 = confirmations/reorgs handling with the finalized-tag policy. The configurable finality policy MUST use the RPC finalized tag as the formal boundary; the unfinalized window is defined as finalized+1 through latest; unfinalized data may be collected and observed but MUST NOT enter the qualified dataset; on finalized unavailable / fallback / abnormal / endpoint ancestry disagreement -> stop qualification (fail closed); automatic fallback to confirmations is forbidden; confirmations=12 is retained only as an EXPERIMENTAL_NOT_LIVE_APPROVED placeholder and MUST NOT support mainnet qualification, paper, or live promotion; tests MUST explicitly inject the finality policy. FINALIZED_ANCESTRY_VIOLATION is defined as: a previously finalized block no longer belongs to the finalized ancestry, or qualified endpoints persistently disagree on finalized block hash/ancestry. On FINALIZED_ANCESTRY_VIOLATION: halt immediately; record an append-only critical-incident candidate; block new backtest qualification, paper, and live decisions; preserve old raw partitions, old canonical generation, and all provider evidence; persist the new fork/observation as new append-only evidence; escalate to the Phase 8 operator/incident workflow; only after a manual incident declaration and reconciliation may a superseding canonical generation be created. Clarify the contract sentence as: > Finalized raw evidence is never rewritten, including during a critical incident. A declared critical incident may authorize creation of a superseding canonical generation after operator review. Companion reason codes: finalized_unavailable / finalized_ancestry_disagreement / finality_tag_unavailable / FINALIZED_ANCESTRY_VIOLATION. T033 owns detection, reason code, halt, and journal; Phase 8 owns manual incident handling and recovery approval. An independent Plan Reviewer must then verify the edits are complete, consistent, and do not weaken acceptance.
